section.title: Firewall
section.intro: Traffic from a higher security level to a lower one is allowed, and its replies come back on their own. Traffic from a lower level to a higher one needs an access list bound to the interface with access-group (Access lists card or the CLI).

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.hint: Give every interface you use a name (nameif) and a level from 0 (least trusted, e.g. outside) to 100 (most trusted). Leave the level empty for the default: 100 for "inside", 0 for any other name.
interfaces.empty: This firewall has no routed interfaces.

rules.title: Equal levels
rules.interInterface: Allow traffic between two interfaces with the same level
rules.interInterfaceHint: Same as same-security-traffic permit inter-interface. Off: equal levels cannot talk to each other.
rules.intraInterface: Allow traffic that leaves by the interface it came in on

icmp.title: Ping (ICMP)
icmp.hint: Lab rule: on by default here, so a ping sent towards a lower level gets its reply back. Real firewalls do not track ping until ICMP inspection is turned on. Off: replies count as new traffic from the lower level and are dropped unless an access list allows them.

timeouts.title: Idle timeouts (seconds)
timeouts.hint: A connection that sees no packet for this long is removed from the table.

connections.title: Open connections
connections.noRuntime: The live connection table is in the console: open the CLI tab and type show conn (clear conn empties it).

port.nameifHint: e.g. inside, outside, dmz. Empty: the interface passes no traffic.
port.levelHint: 0–100. Empty: the default (100 for inside, 0 for other names).

errors.nameifInvalid: A name is one word without spaces.
errors.securityLevelOutOfRange: Enter a whole number from 0 to 100, or leave it empty for the default.
errors.levelNeedsNameif: Give the interface a name first: a level without a name has no effect.

notes.noNameif: Firewall: {{iface}} has no name (nameif), so no traffic passes through it. The packet is dropped.
notes.connectionMatched: Firewall: the packet belongs to connection {{id}} ({{protocol}} {{initiator}} → {{responder}}), so it passes without a level check.
notes.errorMatched: Firewall: this ICMP error is about connection {{id}} ({{protocol}} {{initiator}} → {{responder}}), so it passes.
notes.connectionCreated: Firewall: new {{protocol}} connection {{id}} from {{initiator}} ({{from}}) to {{responder}} ({{to}}). Its replies will pass.
notes.connectionEstablished: Firewall: SYN+ACK came back, connection {{id}} is established.
notes.connectionHalfClosed: Firewall: FIN seen, connection {{id}} is closing.
notes.connectionReset: Firewall: RST seen, connection {{id}} is removed.
notes.higherToLower: Firewall: {{from}} (level {{fromLevel}}) → {{to}} (level {{toLevel}}): from a higher to a lower security level, allowed.
notes.aclException: Firewall: {{from}} (level {{fromLevel}}) → {{to}} (level {{toLevel}}): from a lower to a higher level, allowed because access list {{acl}} is bound inbound on {{from}} and permitted it.
notes.lowerToHigher: Firewall: {{from}} (level {{fromLevel}}) → {{to}} (level {{toLevel}}): from a lower to a higher level, and no access list is bound inbound on {{from}}. The packet is dropped.
notes.sameLevel: Firewall: {{from}} and {{to}} both have level {{level}}, and same-security-traffic does not allow it. The packet is dropped.
notes.sameLevelPermitted: Firewall: {{from}} and {{to}} both have level {{level}}; same-security-traffic allows it.
notes.noConnection: Firewall: a TCP segment ({{flags}}) without SYN that belongs to no connection. The packet is dropped.
